issues.reason: The fixture requires a throwing emplace to make the variant valueless. variant.mod permits that outcome but does not require it. In particular, the old float can be saved and restored after the constructor throws. Throwing constructors of the new alternative do not prevent restoration of the old alternative.

issues.reason: Uses throwing same-alternative emplace as a supposedly guaranteed valueless fixture. Preserving/restoring the old alternative is allowed; its copy constructor in this test does not actually throw.

issues.reason: Requires a free real mutex to be acquired by a single try operation or a fixed finite number of tries. try_lock and the timed try operations may fail spuriously even when ownership is available. The recursive_mutex test also assumes success within 1000 tries.
issues.remedy: Use lock() to establish availability after release, or separate a retry-based quality-of-implementation test from conformance.

issues.reason: After moving, swapping and move-assigning wrappers, requires exactly one destruction before leaving the scope and exactly four overall. The test allows target moves but fails to account for their destructions.
issues.remedy: Require destruction exactly once per constructed target (including move constructions); retain the stricter identity/count checks for the immovable case.

issues.reason: Requires an engine returning its minimum to produce the distribution lower bound exactly. The distribution specifies the output interval and density, not the mapping from an individual engine value. A uniform mapping with reversed bit order can produce a different in-range result.
issues.remedy: Check the result is in [a,b); do not prescribe which input maps to a.

issues.reason: Reads plain directly after ar.store(9), while ar is alive; the atomic_ref access rule applies in freestanding mode too.
issues.remedy: Use ar.load().

issues.remedy: Use ar.load().

issues.reason: The notifier loop waits for the predicate-evaluation counter to equal each of 1 and 2 exactly. Permitted spurious wakes can advance the counter to 3 and throw before the notifier observes the intermediate value. The notifier then loops forever until the watchdog kills an otherwise conforming run.
issues.remedy: Use explicit phase/notification handshakes and break when the future is ready; do not equate evaluations with notifications.
